uncited: It differs from siblings like [Maximum Intensity Projection](902-maximum-intensity-projection.md) by retaining full volumetric compositing rather than projecting scalar extrema, and from [Forward Projection (aTx)](1492-forward-projection-atx.md) by using a slab-based decomposition rather than a full shear-warp factorization.
The method approximates the perspective viewing frustum as a sequence of parallel slabs.
The core inputs are the volume dataset, the camera position, and the view direction.
**Slab Decomposition**: The volume is divided into slabs perpendicular to the view direction.
**Parallel Projection Approximation**: Each slab is rendered using parallel projection techniques.
**Compositing**: The results from the parallel projected slabs are composited together.
The approximation error is bounded by adjusting the slab boundaries based on the analytical error model.
The specific time and memory complexity depend on the number of slabs and the resolution of the volume.
